text:
nishant: Ran a short smoke test on canary-3 with prefetch+kv-cache turned on and a 25% qps spike. Observed ~1.2% soft 429s after ~30s. Kernel handoff logs look weird. Anyone free to eyeball profiler output?

alex: I pulled the perf artifacts. Looks like batch assembly latency spiked and we fell back to the smaller matrix-mul kernel for a bunch of microbatches. KV hit rate dropped ~7% during the spike.

chloe: interesting — did the drop in KV hit rate align with eviction churn? We pushed a prefetch threshold change last week.

alex: eviction churn yes. See snippet from the runtime trace:```
[2026-03-17T13:24:05Z] batch_assemble=12ms kernel_choice=optimized (avg_seq=96)
[2026-03-17T13:24:05Z] batch_assemble=38ms kernel_choice=fallback_small (avg_seq=34)
[2026-03-17T13:24:06Z] kv_evict=5ms prefetch_miss=true
```
Notable that when assembly latency > ~30ms we trigger an optimistic kernel swap to keep tail latency bounded.

nishant: Right — our current heuristic swaps kernel when assembly latency > 25ms. Might be too aggressive when KV miss rate temporarily increases. That explains the perf regression.

kelsey: Did we see any change in token-budget assignment? Could a low token budget be causing smaller microbatches and more kernel swaps?

alex: Token budgets were slightly lower for the canary (we reduced target tokens/sec by 10% to be conservative). That reduced batching headroom. Combined with prefetch misses it cascaded.

chloe: Also the request distribution changed during the spike — more short sequences and fewer long ones, so avg_seq for some batches dropped, hitting the fallback kernel selection code path.

nishant: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) increase token_budget_target by 20% for canary-3 (short-term), 2) add KV-prefetch hysteresis window to avoid reacting to single-cycle miss spikes, 3) raise kernel-swap threshold to 40ms and observe. Thoughts?

alex: +1 for hysteresis. We should also add a cooldown per-GPU so_kernel_swap isn't retriggered rapidly. I can prototype a per-gpu cooldown flag in the admission controller.

kelsey: For rollout, can we A/B the token budget bump vs hysteresis change? One for throughput, one for stability. Need metrics: soft_429_rate, avg_token_cost, p95_latency.

chloe: I collected profiler buckets for the run. p50 batch_assembly went 10ms -> 36ms; p95 went 28ms -> 110ms. KV hit-rate for the canary window: 82% -> 75%.

nishant: Thanks. I'll open a short-lived experiment: canary-3 variant A = token_budget +20%; variant B = prefetch hysteresis(3s) + swap_threshold 40ms + per-GPU cooldown 5s. 1 hour run each, then compare.

infra-bot: deploy: canary-3.A started at 2026-03-17T14:10:10Z by nishant :rocket:
infra-bot: deploy: canary-3.B started at 2026-03-17T14:10:12Z by nishant :rocket:

alex: quick note — add a lightweight trace tag so we can correlate kernel_choice transitions with kv_miss events: `trace:kernel_swap_cause=kv_miss|assembly_latency|token_budget`. That will make analysis easier.

kelsey: Also log admission decisions for soft-rejects: include `tokens_requested`, `tokens_granted`, `kv_prefetch_hit` in the event.

chloe: If variant A reduces soft 429s but increases cost, set a cost cap signal so we can auto-fallback to variant B. We'll need the console metric for `estimated_token_cost_per_minute`.

nishant: Agreed. I'll run both for 1h, then gather p50/p95 latency, soft_429 rate, kv_hit_rate, and cost estimate. If variant B shows similar 429 reduction with lower cost, we'll prefer it and then tweak token budgets cluster-wide.

alex: One more observation from the trace: many of the small microbatches were short due to the client-side batching TTL being 10ms. Could be worth increasing TTL to 15-20ms for this workload to allow larger coalescing. But that impacts client latency. We'll flag as optional in the experiment.

nishant: Good call. I'll add a client-side TTL toggle to the experiment with a small subset (10% traffic). Summary of action items:
- nishant: launch both canary variants and collect metrics (in progress)
- alex: add trace tag + per-GPU cooldown prototype (PR)
- chloe: prepare profiler dashboards and cost estimates
- kelsey: add admission decision fields to logs and wire up alerts for soft_429>0.5%

kelsey: ping me once metrics are in, I'll run the A/B comparison and recommend default. :+1:

nishant: thanks all. Will post results in this thread in ~2h.
